title: Lesson 6: Choosing Models & Providers: Capability Tiers, Routing, and Fallbacks
description: The biggest agent-ops mistake is picking one 'best' model and pointing everything at it. This lesson builds the three-tier capability model, the three jobs of a router, and the fallback chains that keep agents alive when providers fail.

questions.question: What is the difference between a routing destination and a router?
options: A destination runs a request; the router picks which one
A destination decides routing; the router only measures latency
A destination is a local model; a router is a managed service
A destination and a router are two names for the same thing
questions.explanation: A destination is a place a request runs, while the router is the decision layer that chooses among destinations, so calling one provider directly is an integration, not routing.

questions.question: Why is routing by capability tier rather than by model name more durable?
options: Tier names are shorter and easier to type
Tiers hide the cost of every request from the bill
Tiers guarantee that the cheapest available model is always chosen
Tier config can be remapped without touching routing logic
questions.explanation: Names and their relative quality rotate quickly, so separating the stable decision (small, medium, large) from the model it resolves to keeps routing logic valid.

questions.question: What is a fallback chain unable to detect on its own?
options: A request that times out before responding
A rate-limited endpoint enforcing a quota
A successful but confidently wrong answer
questions.explanation: Fallbacks react to transport failures like errors and timeouts; a 200 response carrying a wrong answer looks fine, so catching it needs a separate quality check.
